# Input Validation, Output Encoding and Injection (INP)

All data from outside the trust boundary is untrusted: user input, API responses, files, deep links, QR codes, SAP responses and data from other systems. Validate it where it enters, and use the safe API at the point where it is used (the "sink").

## SCS-INP-01 Validate all input on the server; client validation is for usability only

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: All input MUST be validated on the server against an allow-list of type, length, range, format and permitted values before it is used. Client-side validation MUST also be done for usability, but it is never relied on for security.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Prefer allow-lists (permitted values, patterns) over deny-lists.
- Validate the whole object: reject unknown fields and enforce business rules (for example quantity > 0, date not in the past).

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use request DTOs with data annotations ([Required], [MaxLength], [Range], [RegularExpression]) or FluentValidation. [ApiController] returns 400 automatically.
- .NET 8/9 minimal APIs do not validate automatically; call the validator explicitly or use the .NET 10 AddValidation().
- Reject unknown JSON members: JsonSerializerOptions.UnmappedMemberHandling = JsonUnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow.
- Set a timeout on any Regex applied to untrusted input, or use RegexOptions.NonBacktracking. Never build a regex pattern from input.

Verification: Code review confirms every endpoint has server-side validation. Negative tests send oversized, malformed and unexpected values and expect HTTP 400.

## SCS-INP-02 Parameterize every database query

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every database operation MUST use parameterized queries or an ORM. User-supplied data MUST NEVER be concatenated or interpolated into SQL text. Table, column and sort names that come from input MUST be mapped through an allow-list.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use EF Core with LINQ as the primary data access method.
- For raw SQL use FromSql / ExecuteSql / SqlQuery (interpolated values become parameters). Never pass an interpolated string to FromSqlRaw / ExecuteSqlRaw / SqlQueryRaw (analyzer EF1002).
- Dapper: always pass parameters ("WHERE Email = @Email", new { Email = email }).
- ADO.NET: SqlCommand with SqlParameter; never build CommandText with + or $"...".
- SAP: call RFC/BAPI function modules with typed parameters through the SAP .NET Connector, never by building strings.

Verification: Code review and SAST rule for SQL injection (for example Sonar S3649). Grep for FromSqlRaw, ExecuteSqlRaw, CommandText and rawQuery with string interpolation.

## SCS-INP-03 Encode output for its context to prevent XSS

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Output shown in web pages, WebViews or other interpreters MUST be encoded for its context using the framework's built-in encoding. Raw HTML from user input MUST NEVER be rendered. Built-in encoding MUST NOT be disabled.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Razor encodes by default. Never use Html.Raw, MarkupString or HtmlString on user or third-party data.
- If rich HTML input is required, sanitize with a maintained library (for example HtmlSanitizer) using an allow-list of tags.
- JSON APIs: return application/json with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so browsers do not sniff it as HTML.
- Use encoders from System.Text.Encodings.Web (HtmlEncoder, JavaScriptEncoder, UrlEncoder) when building output by hand.

Verification: Code review greps for Html.Raw, MarkupString, loadHtmlString and innerHTML. DAST / manual XSS test of every field that is shown back to users.

## SCS-INP-04 Build URLs, paths and commands with safe APIs

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: URLs, file paths and operating system commands MUST NOT be built by concatenating user input. Use the platform's URL builders with encoding, resolve and check file paths against a base folder, and pass command arguments as a list without a shell.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Build URLs with UriBuilder / QueryHelpers.AddQueryString and Uri.EscapeDataString.
- Paths: Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(root, Path.GetFileName(name))), then check the result starts with root + separator. Path.Combine returns the input unchanged if it is rooted.
- Processes: ProcessStartInfo with UseShellExecute = false and ArgumentList.Add(...). Never build the Arguments string from input.
- Redirects: use LocalRedirect / Results.LocalRedirect, or check Url.IsLocalUrl. Never Redirect(returnUrl).

Verification: Code review greps for Path.Combine with request data, Process.Start, Redirect(, launchUrl and string-built URIs.

## SCS-INP-05 Deserialize only into fixed, expected types

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Data from requests, files, queues or other systems MUST be deserialized only into fixed DTO types. Serializers that let the payload choose the type MUST NOT be used. XML parsers MUST keep DTD processing and external entity resolution disabled.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use System.Text.Json. Polymorphism only through a [JsonDerivedType] allow-list.
- Never use BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer, LosFormatter, ObjectStateFormatter, or JavaScriptSerializer with SimpleTypeResolver.
- Newtonsoft.Json: TypeNameHandling must stay None.
- XML: do not set DtdProcessing.Parse or a non-null XmlResolver (modern .NET is safe by default).

Verification: Grep for BinaryFormatter, TypeNameHandling, NetDataContractSerializer, DtdProcessing.Parse and XmlUrlResolver.
